territorial_scope.description: California state law applying to covered products used by, processing personal information of, or applied directly to children who reside in California.

evidence.quote: “Child” means a natural person under 18 years of age who resides in this state.

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health
agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Adds the LEAD for Kids Act to California's Business and Professions Code. Creates a Standards Board to set risk tiers for AI products used by children; by July 1, 2028, developers must register covered products, assess risk, report incidents and undergo audits, and prohibited-risk products must be kept from children.
summary.long: Adds the LEAD for Kids Act to California's Business and Professions Code, covering AI systems used by children, used to process children's personal information, or applied directly to children, for children under 18 resident in the state. Creates a nine-member LEAD for Kids Standards Board in the Government Operations Agency, which must by January 1, 2028 adopt regulations on covered-product criteria, four risk levels (prohibited, high, moderate, low), assessments, labels, audits, incident reporting, a public registry and registration fees. Prohibited-risk examples include certain companion chatbots and biometric or emotion-assessment uses; high-risk examples include pupil assessment and advertising targeted to children. From July 1, 2028, developers must register covered products, file risk assessments, provide labels, keep prohibited-risk products from children, report incidents within 30 days, obtain consent before training on children's personal information, and undergo independent audits. Deployers have parallel incident, license-display and consent duties, and developers and deployers may not retaliate against whistleblowers or make misleading compliance statements. The Attorney General may seek a $25,000 civil penalty per violation on Board referral, and a child harmed by a covered product, or a parent, may sue for damages. Penalties fund the LEAD for Kids AI Fund; duplicative requirements under other state risk-assessment laws may be excused.
